This can't merge as designed.  We can't be imposing redfish rules in common layers.  There are interfaces in some of the other layers that use the DateTime key in their strings, so this isn't a hypothetical concern.

If you're on discord, it would be good to talk about options on where this could be put, and I support the usecase itself.

FWIW, this is a "should" in the spec, so bmcweb is technically still in compliance.  Were you seeing real-world performance impacts on this?

One other potential solution that you could implement in your client is to use $select to only select the fields that you are using in your application, and omit DateTime.  That would get you an etag that didn't include datetime.  If you're chasing performance, $select is a good thing to do anyway.
Removed all RF code from HTTP layer
This is a common HTTP layer that applies to all http requests.  We cannot be applying redfish-specific rules in the http protocol layer.
Done

This looks like it's basically reimplemented set/releaseCompleteRequestHandler

I get those APIs aren't the easiest to use, but I would much prefer we improve them rather than add specific callbacks for every possible use case.

?  Any reason we're doing this in a redfish-specific function?  etag is an http concept.

Also, this is only the OEM router, so I suspect this isn't doing what you think it's doing.
Existing code buries `expectedHash` here, breaking if-none-match specifically for resources that use OEM subroutes (managers.hpp).

I'm not following... what do you mean "buries"? I see no mention of expectedHash here.

> breaking if-none-match specifically for resources that use OEM subroutes

Why is that?  The oem sub route will generate a hash, yes, but then when it's rolled up, the hash will be recomputed, right?

`expectedHash` (now renamed `expectedEtag`) comes from the request's if-none-match header; this isn't the etag we compute for the response.  The change is necessary because `multiResp` is newly created here and the expectedEtag value is initialized as empty,  The if-none-match comparison gets called on `multiResp`, so we need to move the value for `expectedEtag` from the original `asyncResp` here to `multiResp`.

I moved this functionality to query_param.hpp `startMultiFragmentHandle` to match where `jsonValue` is also copied from the original Response to the new one.

I'm also not understanding why this needs modified at all.  There are no OEM parameters that get ignored today, so even if this was a data structure issue, this code shouldn't be called for any of the datetime things?

It doesn't really have anything to do with the datetime things, it's just another thing preventing if-none-match from working specifically on this one resource.  Could be a separate PR but I included it here since it's a small change.

Please remove it from this patch and put it in its own commit so it can have its own commit message.  This code isn't a resource, this code is a multi-request aggregator that's used on every resource.

Once it's in its own commit, with a commit message about what problem you're trying to solve, we can go from there on how to actually solve it.
Ack will do

Now that I understand this, this definitely doesn't work because there will be multiple pieces appended in an expand query.  The way you've written it, this one just handles the last expanded one and uses that as the hash.  The order in which they're expanded is not consistent, and the etag needs to apply to the entire resource, not just the last-added member.
This is the incoming etag value from the client's 'if-none-match' header in their request, it's not the etag value that's actually calculated from the content of the response.
